topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture scope on the initiation and resolution of inflammation within the context of the course.

topics.label: Pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the molecular criteria used by the innate immune system to recognize signs of infection and cellular damage while distinguishing self from non-self.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and downstream signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the cellular localization, genetics, and signaling mechanisms of host receptors that detect danger signals to trigger inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Inflammatory cell dynamics and physiological consequences
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how sentinel cell activation orchestrates leukocyte recruitment into tissues, lymphatic fluid trafficking, and potential systemic complications such as septic shock.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation and tissue repair
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation and drive tissue healing, as well as the long-term containment outcomes that arise when inflammation fails to resolve.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing remarks and previews the upcoming lecture on the complement system.
